texts.preamble: Firoj vs Asif Ali on 25 July, 2025 :1: In The Court Of Ms. Charu Gupta Presiding Officer, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-01 (Se), Saket Courts : New Delhi Mact No:148/19 Firoj v. Asif Ali Cnr No.: Dlse01-001337-2019 1. Sh. Firoj S/o Mohd. Iliyas R/o Village Nirpura, Distt-Baghpat, U.P. (through his brother/next friend/ guardian Sh. Irshad Ali) .....Petitioner Versus 1. Sh. Asif Ali S/o Usman R/o Khushal Nagar, Lisari Gate, Meerut, U.P. ............Owner/ Respondent no.1 2. Sh. Abdul Majid S/o Abdul Rehman R/o Village Jaula, Post Khas, Distt-Muzaffarnagar U.P. ............Driver/Respondent no.2 3. Universal Sompo General Insurance Co. Ltd. Through its Manager Office at 5th Floor, Shakuntala Apartment Flat no. 514, 59, Nehru Place New Delhi-110019. ............Insurance company/Respondent no.3 Digitally signed Charu by Charu Gupta Gupta Date: 2025.07.25 17:15:54 +0530 Mact No148/19 Firoj v. Asif Ali P.No. 1 Of 22 Bk Date of accident : 23.11.2018 Result of accident : Injury(Permanent disability) Date of filing of Petition : 22.02.2019 Date of Decision : 25.07.2025 Award 1. The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Sh. Firoj suffered grievous injury.
texts.facts: 1. The present claim petition arises out of road accident in which one Sh. Firoj suffered grievous injury. An application u/s 166(1) MV Act was accordingly filed by the claimant/applicant. Firoj vs Asif Ali on 25 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199646669/ 1 2. Brief facts of the case are that on 23.11.2018 at about 10.30 AM, petitioner was travelling from village Jaula to Subharti hospital, Meerut, U.P. alongwith his sister Smt. Bitto@Tabassum (since deceased in the accident) and niece Humera (since deceased in the accident) on motorcycle bearing no. DL-7S-BW-7435 which was being driven by the petitioner. Brother-in-law of the petitioner namely Anis, alongwith his father Ali Hasan were on another motorcycle. When their motorcycles reached Meerut-Budhana Highway at Bhuni Chauraha near Essar Petrol Pump, a truck bearing no.UP-15DT-0155(hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) coming from Shamli side and driven in a rash and negligent manner, hit the motorcycle of the petitioner from left rear side. Due to the impact, the motorcycle of the petitioner lost its balance. The petitioner's sister and niece got crushed by the offending truck and died on the spot while petitioner sustained grievous injuries. The petitioner, his sister and niece were rushed to District hospital Sururpur where petitioner's sister and niece were declared brought dead. Petitioner was referred to Medical CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.07.25 17:16:05 +0530 MACT NO148/19 Firoj v. Asif Ali P.No. 2 Of 22 BK College Meerut for further treatment and later referred to GTB hospital for higher treatment. 3. On complaint of Anis Ahmad, an FIR bearing no.0407/2018 dated 24.11.18 was registered u/s 279,338,304-A of IPC at PS Sururpur, District Meerut, U.P. Matter was investigated and a chargesheet was filed before concerned criminal court while a claim petition was filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is owner and Respondent no.2 is driver of the offending vehicle. Respondent no.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. 5. Written statement was filed by Respondent no.1 and 2 wherein allegations of negligence on the part of Respondent no.2 have been denied. Though it has not been denied that Respondent no.2 was driving the offending vehicle, it is pleaded that such Respondent was driving the vehicle carefully and in a sensible manner. It has been pleaded that the accident occurred due to sole negligence of the petitioner who was driving his motorcycle rashly and in a negligent manner. No reply/written statement filed by Respondent no.3/ insurance company despite opportunity. 6. Vide order dated 25.11.2019, following issues were framed. 1. Whether injured Firoj suffered injuries in a road accident on 23.11.2018 due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle no. UP-15DT-0155 being driven by R2, owned by R1 and insured with R3 (inadvertently written as driven by R1, owned by R2)? OPP 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to any Digitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.07.25 MACT NO148/19 Firoj v. Asif Ali P.No. 317:16:17 Of 22+0530 BK compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom? OPP. 3. Relief. Firoj vs Asif Ali on 25 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199646669/ 2 7. To prove his claim, petitioner examined his father Sh. Iliyas as PW-1. PW-1 led his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/1. He deposed on the lines of the claim petition and reiterated the allegations stated in the application. He further stated that the petitioner was lastly referred to GTB Hospital, Delhi and continues to be under treatment. He stated that before the accident, his son was working as an electrician and earning Rs.10,000/- p.m. He stated that his son sustained grievous injury on his head, right hand and leg due to which he has become 57% disabled. He stated that claim petitions in respect of death of Bitto and Humera were settled before learned MACT, Baghpat, U.P. He further deposed that Rs.30,000/- had been spent on conveyance and Rs.50,000/- towards attendant for the petitioner. PW-1 relied upon his Aadhar card as Ex.PW-1/A, original prescription and discharge summary as Ex.PW-1/B, certified copy of FIR as Ex.PW-1/C, certified copy of site plan and chargesheet as Ex.PW-1/D, intermediate school marksheet as Ex.PW-1/E, Aadhar card of the petitioner as Ex.PW-1/F, original disability certificate as Ex.PW-1/G and copy of order dated 14.12.2019 as Mark-1. He was cross-examined by Ld. counsel for insurance company/Respondent no.3. Sh. Anees Ahmad (Eye witness) was examined as PW-2 by way of affidavit Ex.PW-2/1. PW-2 stated that on 23.11.2018, he alongwith his father Ali Hasan, was going to Subharti hospital, Meerut on motorcycle bearing no.UP-11BD-5304 for treatment CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA 2025.07.25 Date: 17:16:29 +0530 MACT NO148/19 Firoj v. Asif Ali P.No. 4 Of 22 BK of his wife Bitto@Tabassum. His brother-in-law Firoj S/o Iliyas who was driving motorcycle bearing no.DL-7S-BW-7435, was ahead of the motorcycle of PW-2. Wife of PW-2 Bitto and his daughter Humera were riding with petitioner Firoj. When they reached Meerut-Shamli Highway at Bhuni Chauraha, near Essar Petrol Pump at about 10-10.30 AM, a truck bearing no. UP-15BD-0155 came at a high speed, driven in a rash and negligent manner and hit the motorcycle of the petitioner. Due to the collision, motorcycle of the petitioner got disbalanced, wife and daughter of PW-2 fell from the motorcycle and got crushed by the offending truck. While wife and daughter of PW-2 died on the spot, petitioner Firoj sustained grievous injuries on his head and over his body. The offending truck was apprehended but its driver managed to flee from the spot. All the three injured were taken to District hospital where Bitto and Humera were declared 'brought dead' while petitioner Firoj received treatment. PW-2 stated that he got lodged an FIR at PS Sururpur, District Meerut on 24.11.2018. He further deposed that the accident occurred due to gross negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. He relied upon his Aadhar card as Ex.PW-2/A. He was duly cross-examined by learned counsel for insurance company. No evidence has been led on behalf of the respondents. 8. Final arguments in details were addressed on behalf of the claimant/injured and the insurance company.
texts.arguments: Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. 10. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of charge sheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. Firoj vs Asif Ali on 25 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199646669/ 4 12. Also driver of the offending vehicle has not challenged or denied by evidence, his rashness or negligence in driving of the offending vehicle or committing the accident. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of CHARU Digitally signed by CHARU GUPTA Date: 2025.07.25 GUPTA 17:17:13 +0530 MACT NO148/19 Firoj v. Asif Ali P.No. 7 Of 22 BK offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. 13. 15. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680 . The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 16.6. Observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajkumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. is quoted hereunder: At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: "...... In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". In the case of semi-illiterate claimants, theDigitally signed CHARU by CHARU GUPTA GUPTA Date: 2025.07.25 17:18:58 +0530 MACT NO148/19 Firoj v. Asif Ali P.No. 18 Of 22 BK Tribunal should ordinarily invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit.
